description: Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, is a beloved Indian dish renowned for its incredibly rich, creamy, and subtly sweet tomato-based gravy. Tender pieces of succulent chicken are slow-cooked in a luxurious sauce, infused with aromatic spices and finished with butter and cream. This iconic recipe delivers a comforting and unforgettable culinary experience that is perfect for any special occasion or a delightful family meal.

ingredients.item: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast

ingredients.notes: soaked in warm water for 15 minutes

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with plain yogurt, 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, Kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric powder, garam masala, and salt. Mix well to ensure all chicken pieces are coated. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes, or preferably for 2-4 hours for best flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Marinated Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of butter in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook until the chicken is browned on all sides and cooked through, about 8-10 minutes. Remove the cooked chicken from the pan and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Gravy Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, add another 2 tablespoons of butter. Once melted, add the chopped onion and saute until translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, green cardamom pods, cinnamon stick, and bay leaf. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Stir in the crushed tomatoes and soaked cashews.

instructions.title: Simmer and Blend the Gravy
instructions.text: Bring the tomato mixture to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 10-15 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the tomatoes to soften. Remove from heat and let it cool slightly. Discard the whole spices (cardamom, cinnamon, bay leaf) if desired, or leave them for deeper flavor. Carefully transfer the mixture to a blender and blend until completely smooth. Strain the gravy through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean pan for an extra smooth texture.

instructions.title: Finish the Butter Chicken Gravy
instructions.text: Return the strained gravy to the pan and bring it to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat. Stir in the dried fenugreek leaves (Kasuri Methi), sugar, and the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter. Cook for 2-3 minutes, allowing the butter to melt and the flavors to combine beautifully. Adjust salt and sugar to your preference.

instructions.title: Combine and Serve
instructions.text: Add the cooked chicken pieces to the simmering gravy. Stir gently to coat the chicken thoroughly. Pour in the heavy cream and mix well. Heat through for another 2-3 minutes, ensuring the chicken is warmed through but do not boil after adding cream. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and serve hot with naan bread, rice, or roti.

tips: For truly authentic flavor, use Kashmiri red chili powder which provides a vibrant color without excessive heat. If unavailable, a mix of regular chili powder and paprika can be used.
Soaking cashews before blending is crucial for achieving a super smooth and creamy gravy texture. Do not skip this step.
Always add heavy cream at the very end and avoid boiling the gravy after its addition, as this can cause the cream to curdle. Gently heat through only.
article:
Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani: Your Ultimate Guide to a Beloved Indian Lunch Recipe

There are few dishes in Indian cuisine as universally adored and instantly recognizable as Butter Chicken, also known as Murgh Makhani. This iconic dish, with its rich, creamy tomato gravy and succulent pieces of chicken, has captivated palates worldwide, cementing its place as a staple on restaurant menus and in home kitchens alike. Perfect for a hearty and satisfying Indian lunch, Butter Chicken offers a symphony of flavors – a delicate balance of tanginess from tomatoes, sweetness from cream, and a gentle warmth from aromatic spices, all rounded out by the luxurious touch of butter. If you’ve ever wanted to recreate this culinary masterpiece, or simply learn more about what makes it so special, you’ve come to the right place. Get ready to dive into the world of Murgh Makhani and discover why it’s a dish that truly deserves its legendary status.

## What is Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani?

Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, literally translates to "chicken with butter." Originating in Delhi, India, in the 1950s, it's believed to have been created by Kundan Lal Gujral at Moti Mahal restaurant, the same culinary genius credited with inventing Tandoori Chicken and Dal Makhani. The dish was born from a need to utilize leftover tandoori chicken by simmering it in a rich, tomato-based gravy made with butter and cream. The result was a revelation: a mild, subtly spiced, and incredibly tender chicken dish bathed in a velvety, orange-hued sauce. Unlike many other Indian curries that can be intensely spicy, Butter Chicken is known for its relatively mild profile, making it a favorite for those new to Indian food and a comforting classic for seasoned enthusiasts. Its distinctive flavor comes from a blend of spices like garam masala, fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi), and ginger-garlic, beautifully balanced by the sweetness of tomatoes and the richness of dairy. This makes it an ideal Indian lunch recipe for anyone seeking comfort and flavor.

## Ingredients You Need for Butter Chicken

Crafting the perfect Butter Chicken requires a selection of fresh ingredients and aromatic spices. While the list might seem extensive, most items are readily available and contribute significantly to the dish's signature taste.

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   1.5 lbs boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color, less heat)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1/2 teaspoon garam masala
*   Salt to taste

For the Makhani Sauce:
*   2 tablespoons unsalted butter (plus more for finishing)
*   1 tablespoon oil (vegetable or canola)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   2 tablespoons ginger-garlic paste
*   1 (28-ounce) can crushed tomatoes or pureed fresh tomatoes
*   1/2 cup cashews, soaked in warm water for 15 minutes (optional, but adds richness)
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1/2 teaspoon ground coriander
*   1/4 teaspoon fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi), crushed
*   1/2 cup heavy cream (plus more for garnish)
*   1 tablespoon sugar (or to taste, to balance acidity)
*   Salt to taste
*   Fresh cilantro, chopped (for garnish)

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Butter Chicken

Making homemade Butter Chicken is a rewarding experience. Follow these steps for a delicious outcome:

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients. Mix well, ensuring the chicken is evenly coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours for maximum flavor.
2.  **Cook the Chicken:** Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Cook until lightly browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per side. Set aside.
3.  **Prepare the Sauce Base:** In the same pan, melt 2 tablespoons of butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.
4.  **Build the Flavor:** Add the crushed tomatoes, soaked cashews (if using), red chili powder, garam masala, turmeric, and ground coriander to the pan. Stir well. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes have cooked down and the oil starts to separate.
5.  **Blend the Sauce:** Carefully transfer the sauce mixture to a blender (or use an immersion blender directly in the pot). Blend until completely smooth and creamy. For an extra silken texture, you can pass the blended sauce through a fine-mesh sieve. Return the smooth sauce to the pan.
6.  **Finish the Sauce:** Stir in the heavy cream, crushed kasoori methi, sugar, and salt to taste. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer.
7.  **Combine and Serve:** Add the cooked chicken pieces to the sauce. Stir to coat thoroughly and let it simmer for another 5-10 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the chicken to heat through. Before serving, stir in an extra knob of butter for that classic rich finish. Garnish with a swirl of fresh cream and chopped cilantro.

## Pro Tips for the Best Butter Chicken Results

To elevate your Butter Chicken from good to absolutely phenomenal, consider these expert tips:

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marination time. The longer the chicken marinates, the more tender and flavorful it will be. Overnight marination is ideal.
*   **Charred Chicken Adds Depth:** For an authentic restaurant-style flavor, lightly char the marinated chicken. You can do this by grilling it, broiling it in the oven, or even pan-frying until slightly browned on the edges. The smoky notes add a wonderful dimension to the final dish.
*   **Blend Until Silky Smooth:** A hallmark of great Murgh Makhani is its incredibly smooth sauce. Use a high-speed blender and blend until there are no lumps. Straining through a fine-mesh sieve is an extra step that makes a noticeable difference.
*   **Kasoori Methi is a Must:** Don't skip the fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi). Rub them between your palms before adding to release their aromatic oils. They provide a unique, slightly bitter-sweet note that is essential to the Butter Chicken flavor profile.
*   **Balance the Flavors:** Taste your sauce frequently. Adjust the sugar to balance the acidity of the tomatoes, and add salt as needed. A perfectly balanced sauce is the secret to a memorable Butter Chicken.
*   **Good Quality Butter and Cream:** Since these are core ingredients, using high-quality unsalted butter and full-fat heavy cream will result in a richer, more luxurious sauce.

## Serving Suggestions for Murgh Makhani

Butter Chicken is a versatile dish that pairs wonderfully with a variety of accompaniments, making it a perfect Indian lunch spread.

*   **Bread is Essential:** The rich, creamy sauce of Murgh Makhani is just begging to be scooped up with fresh Indian breads. Warm naan bread (plain, garlic, or butter naan) is a classic choice. Roti, paratha, or even simple chapati also work beautifully.
*   **Rice for Soaking Up:** Fluffy basmati rice is an excellent complement, providing a neutral canvas for the vibrant flavors of the curry. Jeera rice (cumin rice) or a simple pilaf would also be delicious.
*   **Cooling Sides:** To balance the richness, offer some cooling side dishes. A simple cucumber raita (yogurt with grated cucumber and spices) or a fresh kachumber salad (diced onion, tomato, cucumber with lemon juice) adds a refreshing contrast.
*   **Pickles and Chutneys:** A small dollop of mango pickle or a sweet tamarind chutney can add an extra layer of flavor and zest to your meal.

## Variations and Substitutions for Butter Chicken

While the classic Butter Chicken recipe is divine, there are many ways to adapt it to dietary preferences or available ingredients.

*   **Vegetarian Butter "Chicken":** For a delicious vegetarian twist, substitute chicken with paneer (Indian cottage cheese), tofu, chickpeas, or mixed vegetables like cauliflower and peas. Marinate paneer or tofu similarly to chicken for added flavor.
*   **Lighter Version:** To reduce the calorie count, you can use low-fat yogurt in the marinade and opt for half-and-half or light cream instead of heavy cream in the sauce. You can also reduce the amount of butter, though some will be needed for flavor.
*   **Nut-Free Option:** If you have a nut allergy, you can omit the cashews. To maintain a creamy texture, you can add a tablespoon of poppy seeds (soaked and ground) or a bit of ground almonds (if not allergic to other nuts) or simply rely on the cream for richness.
*   **Spice Level Adjustment:** For those who prefer more heat, increase the amount of red chili powder or add a finely chopped green chili during the sautéing of the onions. For less heat, reduce the chili powder or use only Kashmiri chili for color.
*   **Smoky Flavor:** To impart a smoky flavor without a tandoor, place a small, heat-proof bowl in the finished curry. Heat a piece of charcoal until red hot, place it in the bowl, drizzle a teaspoon of ghee or oil over it, and quickly cover the pot for 5-10 minutes.

Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is more than just a dish; it's an experience. Its comforting flavors and creamy texture make it an irresistible choice for any meal, especially a satisfying Indian lunch. Whether you're a seasoned chef or a home cook eager to explore Indian cuisine, this guide provides everything you need to create a truly memorable rendition of this beloved classic. So gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare to be delighted by the magic of homemade Butter Chicken!
